articles.title: 完型 · 网络匿名与可信身份
articles.context: 网络匿名、网络犯罪与可信身份体系。语气理性审慎，突出隐私与安全之间的张力。
rows: The Internet affords anonymity to its users, a blessing to privacy and freedom of speech.
互联网让使用者可以匿名，这既保护隐私，也保障言论自由。
explain
But that very anonymity is also behind the explosion of cyber-crime that has swept across the Web.
然而，正是这种匿名性也助长了席卷网络的网络犯罪。
explain
Can privacy be preserved while bringing safety and security to a world that seems increasingly lawless ?
问题在于：在一个似乎越来越缺乏规则约束的世界里，能否一边保住隐私，一边带来安全与保障？
explain

Last month, Howard Schmidt, the nation’s cyber-czar, offered the federal government a proposal to make the Web a safer place – a “voluntary trusted identity” system that would be the high-tech equivalent of a physical key, a fingerprint and a photo ID card, all rolled into one.
上个月，美国“网络事务主管”霍华德·施密特向联邦政府提出一项建议，希望让网络更安全——建立一种“自愿的可信身份”体系。它相当于把实体钥匙、指纹和带照片的身份证的功能合为一体的高科技版本。
explain
The system might use a smart identity card, or a digital credential linked to a specific computer, and would authenticate users at a range of online services.
这个体系可以采用智能身份卡，或与特定电脑绑定的数字凭证，并能在多种在线服务中验证用户身份。
explain
The idea is to create a federation of private online identity systems.
其思路是创建一个由多个私人在线身份系统组成的联盟。
explain
Users could select which system to join, and only registered users whose identities have been authenticated could navigate those systems.
用户可以自行选择加入哪个系统，而只有身份得到认证的注册用户才能在这些系统中活动。
explain
The approach contrasts with one that would require an Internet driver’s license issued by the government.
这与由政府签发“互联网驾照”的做法形成对照。
explain
Google and Microsoft are among companies that already have these “single sign-on” systems that make it possible for users to log in just once but use many different services.
谷歌、微软等公司已经拥有类似的“单点登录”系统，使用户只需登录一次，就能使用多项服务。
explain

In effect , the approach would create a “walled garden” in cyberspace, with safe “neighborhoods” and bright “streetlights” to establish a sense of a trusted community. Mr. Schmidt described it as a “voluntary ecosystem” in which “individuals and organizations can complete online transactions with confidence , trusting the identities of each other and the identities of the infrastructure on which the transaction runs.”
实际上，这种做法会在网络空间形成一个“有围墙的花园”：其中有安全的“社区”和明亮的“路灯”，从而建立可信社区的感觉。施密特把它称为一种“自愿生态系统”，在其中，个人和组织能够有把握地完成网上交易，因为彼此的身份以及承载交易的基础设施身份都是可信的。
explain
Still, the administration’s plan has divided privacy rights activists.
尽管如此，政府的方案仍使隐私权活动人士意见分化：
explain
Some applaud the approach; others are concerned.
有人赞同，也有人担忧。
explain
It seems clear that such a scheme is an initiative push toward what would eventually be a compulsory Internet “driver’s license” mentality.
显然，这样的方案可能逐步把人们推向一种最终强制实行“互联网驾照”的思维。
explain

The plan has also been greeted with skepticism by some computer security experts, who worry that the “voluntary ecosystem” envisioned by Mr. Schmidt would still leave much of the Internet vulnerable .
部分计算机安全专家也以怀疑态度看待该计划，他们担心施密特设想的“自愿生态系统”仍会让互联网的大部分区域处于脆弱状态。
explain
They argue that all Internet users should be forced to register and identify themselves, in the same way that drivers must be licensed to drive on public roads.
他们主张所有互联网用户都应被强制注册并表明身份，就像司机必须取得驾照才能在公共道路上驾驶一样。
explain

articles.title: 阅读一 · 外部董事为何提前离场
articles.context: 公司治理与外部董事的声誉激励。朗读保持分析感，数据处清晰克制。
rows: Ruth Simmons joined Goldman Sachs’s board as an outside director in January 2000; a year later she became president of Brown University.
露丝·西蒙斯2000年1月以外部董事身份加入高盛董事会，一年后出任布朗大学校长。
explain
For the rest of the decade she apparently managed both roles without attracting much criticism.
在此后的大部分时间里，她似乎同时兼顾两个职位，并未招致多少批评。
explain
But by the end of 2009 Ms. Simmons was under fire for having sat on Goldman’s compensation committee; how could she have let those enormous bonus payouts pass unremarked?
但到2009年底，她因曾担任高盛薪酬委员会成员而受到抨击：那些巨额奖金发放，她怎么会听之任之、毫无异议？
explain
By February the next year Ms. Simmons had left the board.
第二年2月，她离开了董事会，
explain
The position was just taking up too much time, she said.
并称这个职位占用了太多时间。
explain
Outside directors are supposed to serve as helpful, yet less biased, advisers on a firm’s board.
外部董事本应在公司董事会中充当有帮助、同时相对不偏不倚的顾问。
explain
Having made their wealth and their reputations elsewhere, they presumably have enough independence to disagree with the chief executive’s proposals.
他们的财富和声誉通常来自别处，理论上应有足够独立性去反对首席执行官的提议。
explain
If the sky, and the share price is falling, outside directors should be able to give advice based on having weathered their own crises.
当形势恶化、股价下跌时，他们也应凭借自己曾渡过危机的经验提出建议。
explain
The researchers from Ohio University used a database that covered more than 10,000 firms and more than 64,000 different directors between 1989 and 2004.
俄亥俄大学的研究人员利用一个数据库，研究了1989至2004年间一万多家公司、六万四千多名董事，
explain
Then they simply checked which directors stayed from one proxy statement to the next.
并简单核查哪些董事会成员会从一份委托书持续留任到下一份。
explain
The most likely reason for departing a board was age, so the researchers concentrated on those “surprise” disappearances by directors under the age of 70.
离开董事会最常见的原因是年龄，因此研究人员把注意力集中在70岁以下董事“意外”离任的情况上。
explain
They found that after a surprise departure, the probability that the company will subsequently have to restate earnings increases by nearly 20%.
他们发现，董事意外离任后，公司随后重述财务收益的概率上升近20%；
explain
The likelihood of being named in a federal class-action lawsuit also increases, and the stock is likely to perform worse.
公司被列入联邦集体诉讼的可能性也会上升，股票表现也往往更差，
explain
The effect tended to be larger for larger firms.
而且大型公司中的这种效应更明显。
explain
Although a correlation between them leaving and subsequent bad performance at the firm is suggestive, it does not mean that such directors are always jumping off a sinking ship.
虽然董事离任与公司之后表现不佳之间存在相关性，但这并不意味着他们总是在“跳离沉船”。
explain
Often they “trade up,” leaving riskier, smaller firms for larger and more stable firms.
很多时候，他们是在“向上换位”：离开风险较高的小公司，转去规模更大、更稳定的公司。
explain

But the researchers believe that outside directors have an easier time of avoiding a blow to their reputations if they leave a firm before bad news breaks, even if a review of history shows they were on the board at the time any wrongdoing occurred.
不过研究人员认为，如果外部董事能在坏消息爆发之前离开公司，就更容易避免自己的声誉受损，即使事后回顾发现，他们在违规行为发生时其实已经身处董事会。
explain
Firms who want to keep their outside directors through tough times may have to create incentives.
那些希望外部董事在困难时期仍留下来的公司，也许必须设计相应激励；
explain
Otherwise outside directors will follow the example of Ms. Simmons, once again very popular on campus.
否则，外部董事就可能效仿西蒙斯——重新成为校园里颇受欢迎的人物。
explain

articles.title: 阅读二 · 报纸真的会消亡吗
articles.context: 传统报业在衰退中的自救与商业模式变化。语气从危机感逐步转向冷静判断。
rows: Whatever happened to the death of newspapers?
“报纸之死”后来怎么样了？
explain
A year ago the end seemed near.
一年前，看起来末日将近。
explain
The recession threatened to remove the advertising and readers that had not already fled to the internet.
经济衰退威胁着报纸的广告收入和读者，而其中相当一部分早已流向互联网。
explain
Newspapers like the San Francisco Chronicle were chronicling their own doom.
像《旧金山纪事报》这样的报纸甚至仿佛在记录自己的消亡。
explain
America’s Federal Trade Commission launched a round of talks about how to save newspapers.
美国联邦贸易委员会还组织了一轮讨论，研究如何拯救报纸：
explain
Should they become charitable corporations?
是否应该把报纸改成慈善性质的公司？
explain
Should the state subsidize them?
政府是否应给予补贴？
explain
It will hold another meeting soon.
委员会很快还会再次开会。
explain
But the discussions now seem out of date.
然而如今这些讨论似乎已经过时。
explain
In much of the world there is little sign of crisis.
在世界许多地方，几乎看不到危机迹象。
explain
German and Brazilian papers have shrugged off the recession.
德国和巴西的报纸已经顶住了衰退。
explain
Even American newspapers, which inhabit the most troubled corner of the global industry, have not only survived but often returned to profit.
就连处于全球报业最困难角落的美国报纸，也不仅活了下来，而且往往重新实现盈利。
explain
Not the 20% profit margins that were routine a few years ago, but profit all the same.
利润率当然不再是几年前司空见惯的20%，但毕竟还是利润。
explain
It has not been much fun.
这个过程一点也不好受。
explain
Many papers stayed afloat by pushing journalists overboard.
许多报纸靠大幅裁减记者才勉强维持。
explain
The American Society of News Editors reckons that 13,500 newsroom jobs have gone since 2007.
美国新闻编辑协会估计，自2007年以来，新闻编辑部已经减少了1.35万个岗位。
explain
Readers are paying more for slimmer products.
读者花的钱更多，拿到的报纸却更薄；
explain
Some papers even had the nerve to refuse delivery to distant suburbs.
一些报纸甚至敢于停止向偏远郊区送报。
explain
Yet these desperate measures have proved the right ones and, sadly for many journalists, they can be pushed further.
不过事实证明，这些孤注一掷的措施是有效的，而且很遗憾，对许多记者来说，这种收缩还可以继续。
explain
Newspapers are becoming more balanced businesses, with a healthier mix of revenues from readers and advertisers.
报纸的商业结构正在变得更均衡，来自读者和广告商的收入组合也更健康。
explain
American papers have long been highly unusual in their reliance on ads.
美国报纸长期以来高度依赖广告，这在世界上很不寻常。
explain
Fully 87% of their revenues came from advertising in 2008, according to the Organization for Economic Cooperation & Development (OECD).
经合组织数据显示，2008年美国报纸87%的收入来自广告，
explain
In Japan the proportion is 35%.
而日本这一比例只有35%，
explain
Not surprisingly, Japanese newspapers are much more stable.
难怪日本报业稳定得多。
explain
The whirlwind that swept through newsrooms harmed everybody, but much of the damage has been concentrated in areas where newspapers are least distinctive.
席卷编辑部的风暴伤及所有人，但损失主要集中在报纸最缺乏独特性的领域：
explain
Car and film reviewers have gone.
汽车和电影评论员消失了，
explain
So have science and general business reporters.
科学记者和一般商业记者也减少了，
explain
Foreign bureaus have been savagely cut off.
海外记者站更是遭到大幅削减。
explain
Newspapers are less complete as a result.
因此报纸不再那么“包罗万象”。
explain
But completeness is no longer a virtue in the newspaper business.
但在今天的报业中，完整全面已经不再是一种优势。
explain

articles.title: 阅读三 · “少即是多”的住宅美学
articles.context: 战后美国住宅设计与“少即是多”理念。语气平稳，建筑史人物和例证处稍作停顿。
rows: We tend to think of the decades immediately following World War II as a time of prosperity and growth, with soldiers returning home by the millions, going off to college on the G. I. Bill and lining up at the marriage bureaus.
我们往往把二战结束后的几十年想象成繁荣与增长的年代：数以百万计的士兵返乡，凭《军人权利法案》进入大学，并在婚姻登记处排起长队。
explain
But when it came to their houses, it was a time of common sense and a belief that less could truly be more.
但说到住房，那却是一个崇尚常识、相信“少也可以真正成为多”的时代。
explain

During the Depression and the war, Americans had learned to live with less, and that restraint, in combination with the postwar confidence in the future, made small, efficient housing positively stylish.
经历大萧条和战争之后，美国人学会了用更少资源生活；这种克制，加上战后对未来的信心，使小巧、高效的住房反而变得时髦。
explain
Economic condition was only a stimulus for the trend toward efficient living.
经济条件只是推动高效生活趋势的一个刺激因素。
explain

The phrase “less is more” was actually first popularized by a German, the architect Ludwig Mies van der Rohe, who like other people associated with the Bauhaus, a school of design, emigrated to the United States before World War II and took up posts at American architecture schools.
“少即是多”这句话最初真正流行起来，是由于德国建筑师路德维希·密斯·凡·德·罗。他与包豪斯设计学院的其他相关人士一样，在二战前移居美国，并在美国建筑院校任职。
explain
These designers came to exert enormous influence on the course of American architecture, but none more so than Mies.
这批设计师对美国建筑的发展产生了巨大影响，其中尤以密斯最突出。
explain
Mies’s signature phrase means that less decoration, properly organized, has more impact than a lot.
密斯的标志性说法意味着：如果组织得当，较少的装饰反而比大量装饰更有力量。
explain
Elegance, he believed, did not derive from abundance.
他认为，优雅并不来自繁多。
explain
Like other modern architects, he employed metal, glass and laminated wood – materials that we take for granted today but that in the 1940s symbolized the future.
像其他现代主义建筑师一样，他使用金属、玻璃和层压木材——这些材料如今习以为常，但在20世纪40年代象征着未来。
explain
Mies’s sophisticated presentation masked the fact that the spaces he designed were small and efficient, rather than big and often empty.
密斯精致的呈现方式掩盖了一个事实：他设计的空间通常小而高效，而不是大而空旷。
explain

The apartments in the elegant towers Mies built on Chicago’s Lake Shore Drive, for example, were smaller – two-bedroom units under 1,000 square feet – than those in their older neighbors along the city’s Gold Coast.
例如，他在芝加哥湖滨大道建造的优雅高层公寓，比城市黄金海岸上那些老邻居的住宅更小——两居室不足1000平方英尺。
explain

But they were popular because of their airy glass walls, the views they afforded and the elegance of the buildings’ details and proportions, the architectural equivalent of the abstract art so popular at the time.
但这些公寓很受欢迎，因为有通透的玻璃墙、开阔的景观，以及建筑细节和比例上的优雅；它们在建筑上的效果，就像当时流行的抽象艺术。
explain
The trend toward “less” was not entirely foreign.
“更少”的趋势也并非完全来自国外。
explain

In the 1930s Frank Lloyd Wright started building more modest and efficient houses – usually around 1,200 square feet – than the spreading two-story ones he had designed in the 1890s and the early 20th century.
20世纪30年代，弗兰克·劳埃德·赖特开始建造更朴素、更高效的住宅，通常约1200平方英尺，比他在19世纪90年代和20世纪初设计的铺展式两层住宅更小。
explain
The “Case Study Houses” commissioned from talented modern architects by California Arts & Architecture magazine between 1945 and 1962 were yet another homegrown influence on the “less is more” trend.
1945至1962年间，《加州艺术与建筑》杂志邀请才华出众的现代建筑师设计的“案例研究住宅”，则成为“少即是多”趋势的另一股本土力量。
explain
Aesthetic effect came from the landscape, new materials and forthright detailing.
它们的审美效果来自景观、新材料和坦率直接的细部处理。
explain

In his Case Study House, Ralph Rapson may have mispredicted just how the mechanical revolution would impact everyday life – few American families acquired helicopters, though most eventually got clothes dryers – but his belief that self-sufficiency was both desirable and inevitable was widely shared.
在自己的案例研究住宅中，拉尔夫·拉普森也许错误预言了机械革命会如何影响日常生活——很少有美国家庭真正拥有直升机，虽然多数家庭后来都有了烘干机——但他关于自给自足既可取又不可避免的信念，当时却得到广泛认同。
explain

articles.title: 阅读四 · 欧元危机与欧洲整合
articles.context: 欧元区危机与德法政策分歧。语气严谨，区分德国方案、法国方案与作者结论。
rows: Will the European Union make it?
欧盟能挺过去吗？
explain
The question would have sounded strange not long ago.
不久以前，这个问题听上去还很奇怪。
explain
Now even the project’s greatest cheerleaders talk of a continent facing a “Bermuda triangle” of debt, population decline and lower growth.
如今，就连欧洲一体化计划最热情的支持者也开始谈论一个正面临“百慕大三角”的大陆：债务、人口下降和低增长。
explain
As well as those chronic problems, the EU faces an acute crisis in its economic core, the 16 countries that use the single currency.
除了这些长期问题，欧盟的经济核心——使用单一货币的16个国家——还面临一场急性危机。
explain

Markets have lost faith that the euro zone’s economies, weaker or stronger, will one day converge thanks to the discipline of sharing a single currency, which denies uncompetitive members the quick fix of devaluation.
市场已经不再相信，无论强弱，欧元区经济体最终都会因为共同使用一种货币而趋同；共同货币所带来的纪律，也剥夺了缺乏竞争力的成员国通过货币贬值迅速解困的办法。
explain
Yet the debate about how to save Europe’s single currency from disintegration is stuck.
然而，如何阻止欧洲单一货币解体的讨论却陷入僵局。
explain
It is stuck because the euro zone’s dominant powers, France and Germany, agree on the need for greater harmonisation within the euro zone, but disagree about what to harmonise.
原因在于欧元区的两大主导力量法国和德国都同意需要在欧元区内部加强协调，却不同意究竟该协调什么。
explain
Germany thinks the euro must be saved by stricter rules on borrowing, spending and competitiveness, backed by quasi-automatic sanctions for governments that do not obey.
德国认为，要挽救欧元，必须对借贷、支出和竞争力实行更严格规则，并对不守规则的政府施加近乎自动的制裁。
explain
These might include threats to freeze EU funds for poorer regions and EU mega-projects, and even the suspension of a country’s voting rights in EU ministerial councils.
这些制裁可以包括冻结对贫困地区和欧盟大型项目的资金，甚至暂停某国在欧盟部长理事会中的投票权。
explain

It insists that economic co-ordination should involve all 27 members of the EU club, among whom there is a small majority for free-market liberalism and economic rigour; in the inner core alone, Germany fears, a small majority favour French interference.
德国坚持认为，经济协调应涵盖欧盟全部27个成员国，因为在这一整体中，自由市场主义和经济纪律尚有微弱多数；德国担心，如果只在内圈协调，支持法国式干预的力量反而会形成微弱多数。
explain
A “southern” camp headed by France wants something different: “European economic government” within an inner core of euro-zone members.
以法国为首的“南方”阵营想要的是另一套方案：在欧元区核心成员之间建立“欧洲经济政府”。
explain

Translated, that means politicians intervening in monetary policy and a system of redistribution from richer to poorer members, via cheaper borrowing for governments through common Eurobonds or complete fiscal transfers.
翻译成具体政策，就是政治家干预货币政策，并建立由富国向穷国再分配的机制，包括通过共同发行欧元债券降低政府融资成本，或者直接进行财政转移。
explain

Finally, figures close to the Franch government have murmured, euro-zone members should agree to some fiscal and social harmonisation: e.g., curbing competition in corporate-tax rates or labour costs.
最后，与法国政府关系密切的人士还提出，欧元区成员国应在财政和社会政策上进行一定协调，例如限制企业税率或劳动力成本方面的竞争。
explain
It is too soon to write off the EU.
现在就断言欧盟失败还为时过早。
explain
It remains the world’s largest trading block.
它仍然是世界最大的贸易集团。
explain

At its best, the European project is remarkably liberal: built around a single market of 27 rich and poor countries, its internal borders are far more open to goods, capital and labour than any comparable trading area.
欧洲一体化计划最好的一面，其实相当自由主义：一个由27个贫富不同国家组成的单一市场，内部边界对商品、资本和劳动力的开放程度，远高于其他任何类似贸易区。
explain
It is an ambitious attempt to blunt the sharpest edges of globalisation, and make capitalism benign.
它是一项雄心勃勃的尝试，意在磨平全球化最尖锐的棱角，使资本主义变得更温和。
explain

articles.title: 新题型 · 公共健康与垃圾食品监管
articles.context: 公共健康监管、肥胖与快餐营销。多位专家发言，整体保持新闻报道式节奏。
rows: Leading doctors today weigh in on the debate over the government’s role in promoting public health by demanding that ministers impose “fat taxes” on unhealthy food and introduce cigarette-style warnings to children about the dangers of a poor diet.
如今，医学界重量级人物加入了关于政府应在促进公共健康中扮演何种角色的争论。他们要求部长们对不健康食品征收“脂肪税”，并像香烟警示那样，提醒儿童不良饮食的危险。
explain

The demands follow comments made last week by the health secretary, Andrew Lansley, who insisted the government could not force people to make healthy choices and promised to free businesses from public health regulations.
这些要求紧随卫生大臣安德鲁·兰斯利上周的言论而来。兰斯利坚持认为，政府不能强迫人们作出健康选择，并承诺让企业摆脱公共卫生方面的监管。
explain

But senior medical figures want to stop fast-food outlets opening near schools, restrict advertising of products high in fat, salt or sugar, and limit sponsorship of sports events by fast-food producers such as McDonald’s.
但资深医学人士希望阻止快餐店在学校附近开业，限制高脂、高盐或高糖食品的广告，并限制麦当劳等快餐企业赞助体育赛事。
explain
They argue that government action is necessary to curb Britain’s addiction to unhealthy food and help halt spiraling rates of obesity, diabetes and heart disease.
他们认为，政府有必要采取行动，抑制英国人对不健康食品的依赖，并遏制肥胖、糖尿病和心脏病率不断攀升。
explain

Professor Terence Stephenson, president of the Royal College of Paediatrics and Child Health, said that the consumption of unhealthy food should be seen to be just as damaging as somking or excessive drinking.
英国皇家儿科与儿童健康学院院长特伦斯·斯蒂芬森教授指出，食用不健康食品的危害应被视为与吸烟或过量饮酒同样严重。
explain
“Thirty years ago, it would have been inconceivable to have imagined a ban on smoking in the workplace or in pubs, and yet that is what we have now.
他说：“三十年前，人们几乎无法想象会禁止在工作场所或酒吧吸烟，可如今这已经成为现实。
explain
Are we willing to be just as courageous in respect of obesity?
面对肥胖问题，我们愿不愿意表现出同样的勇气？
explain
I would suggest that we should be,” said the leader of the UK’s children’s doctors.
我认为应该。”
explain
Lansley has alarmed health campaigners by suggesting he wants industry rather than government to take the lead.
兰斯利则因暗示希望由行业而非政府主导而令健康倡导者不安。
explain
He said that manufacturers of crisps and candies could play a central role in the Change4Life campaign, the centrepiece of government efforts to boost healthy eating and fitness.
他认为，薯片和糖果生产商可以在Change4Life运动中发挥核心作用，这项运动是政府推动健康饮食和健身的核心项目。
explain

He has also criticised the celebrity chef Jamie Oliver’s high-profile attempt to improve school lunches in England as an example of how “lecturing” people was not the best way to change their behaviour.
他还批评名厨杰米·奥利弗高调改善英格兰学校午餐的尝试，认为“说教”并不是改变人们行为的最佳办法。
explain
Stephenson suggested potential restrictions could include banning TV advertisements for foods high in fat, salt or sugar before 9 pm and limiting them on billboards or in cinemas.
斯蒂芬森提出，潜在限制可以包括晚上9点前禁止播放高脂、高盐或高糖食品的电视广告，并限制这类广告出现在广告牌和电影院中。
explain

“If we were really bold, we might even begin to think of high-calorie fast food in the same way as cigarettes – by setting strict limits on advertising, product placement and sponsorship of sports events,” he said.
他还表示：“如果我们真的足够大胆，甚至可以开始像对待香烟那样对待高热量快餐——严格限制广告、产品植入以及体育赛事赞助。”
explain
Such a move could affect firms such as McDonald’s, which sponsors the youth coaching scheme run by the Football Association.
这类措施可能影响麦当劳等企业，因为麦当劳赞助英格兰足球总会运营的青少年教练项目。
explain
Fast-food chains should also stop offering “inducements” such as toys, cute animals and mobile phone credit to lure young customers, Stephenson said.
斯蒂芬森还说，快餐连锁店也应停止用玩具、可爱动物形象、手机话费等“诱因”吸引年轻消费者。
explain

Professor Dinesh Bhugra, president of the Royal College of Psychiatrists, said: “If children are taught about the impact that food has on their growth, and that some things can harm, at least information is available up front.”
英国皇家精神科医学院院长迪内什·布格拉教授说：“如果让孩子了解食物如何影响生长，以及某些东西会带来伤害，至少他们能事先掌握信息。”
explain
He also urged councils to impose “fast-food-free zones” around schools and hospitals – areas within which takeaways cannot open.
他还敦促地方议会在学校和医院周围设立“无快餐区”，禁止外卖店在其中开业。
explain
A Department of Health spokesperson said: “We need to create a new vision for public health where all of society works together to get healthy and live longer.
卫生部发言人表示：“我们需要建立一种新的公共健康愿景，让全社会共同努力，变得更健康、活得更长。
explain
This includes creating a new ‘responsibility deal’ with business, built on social responsibility, not state regulation.
这包括与企业建立新的‘责任协议’，以社会责任而非国家监管为基础。
explain
Later this year, we will publish a white paper setting out exactly how we will achieve this.”
今年晚些时候，我们会发布白皮书，详细说明如何实现这一目标。”
explain
The food industry will be alarmed that such senior doctors back such radical moves, especially the call to use some of the tough tactics that have been deployed against smoking over the last decade.
这些资深医生支持如此激进的措施，尤其是主张采用过去十年对付吸烟时使用的一些强硬手段，势必会让食品行业感到震惊。
explain

articles.title: 翻译 · IT产业的碳排放
articles.context: IT行业碳排放与节能。语气清楚、简洁，数据和因果关系处加强逻辑重音。
rows: Who would have thought that, globally, the IT industry produces about the same volume of greenhouse gases as the world’s airlines do – roughly 2 percent of all CO2 emissions?
谁能想到，从全球范围看，信息技术产业产生的温室气体总量，竟与全球航空业大体相当——约占全部二氧化碳排放量的2%？
explain
Many everyday tasks take a surprising toll on the environment.
许多日常活动对环境造成的负担远超人们想象。
explain
A Google search can leak between 0.2 and 7.0 grams of CO2, depending on how many attempts are needed to get the “right” answer.
一次谷歌搜索可能排放0.2至7.0克二氧化碳，具体取决于要尝试多少次才能得到“正确”答案。
explain
To deliver results to its users quickly, then, Google has to maintain vast data centres around the world, packed with powerful computers.
为了迅速向用户返回结果，谷歌必须在世界各地维持规模庞大的数据中心，里面布满高性能计算机。
explain
While producing large quantities of CO2, these computers emit a great deal of heat, so the centres need to be well air-conditioned, which uses even more energy.
这些计算机在产生大量二氧化碳的同时，也释放大量热量，因此数据中心必须保持良好空调，而这又会消耗更多能源。
explain
However, Google and other big tech providers monitor their efficiency closely and make improvements.
不过，谷歌和其他大型科技服务商会密切监控自身效率，并不断改进。
explain
Monitoring is the first step on the road to reduction, but there is much more to be done, and not just by big companies.
监测是走向减排的第一步，但仍有大量工作要做，而且责任并不只在大公司。
explain
